title: Apple Sales Rise 16% in June Quarter to Record $109 Billion, Services Revenue Falls Short of Forecasts
description:
Apple turned in another solid earnings report overall for the June 2026 quarter, which marks the last earnings period for outgoing CEO Tim Cook.

	F
body:
Apple turned in another solid earnings report overall for the June 2026 quarter, which marks the last earnings period for outgoing CEO Tim Cook.

	For the three months ended June 27, Apple’s Q3 of fiscal 2026, the tech giant reported total revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16%. Net income came in at $29.8 billion, an increase of 27%, translating to diluted earnings per share of $2.02. The results topped Wall Street expectations.


	Apple’s earnings included a favorable impact of 11 cents per from tariff refunds, lifting its EPS by 5%. That came after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s previously implemented global tariffs policy in February.
	

	Helping drive the top line again was Apple’s services business, which turned in a new quarterly revenue record with $30.7 billion (up 12.1%). However, financial analysts were expecting a stronger showing, forecasting $31.22 billion in sales. The services segment includes the App Store, Apple TV, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare, iCloud and advertising.

	The company’s core iPhone biz turned in better-than-expected growth, up 22% to $54.3 billion for the June quarter.

	Cook will step down as Apple CEO after 15 years as of Sept. 1, when John Ternus, senior VP of hardware engineering, will succeed him in the role. Cook will become executive chairman of Apple’s board.

	“Today, Apple is proud to report our strongest June quarter ever, with double-digit revenue growth across iPhone, Mac and Services, and in every geographic segment,” said Cook in prepared remarks.

	For the June quarter, Wall Street analysts had expected overall revenue of $108.65 billion and earnings per share of $1.89, according to data provider LSEG.
	

	(Pictured above: Apple’s John Ternus and Tim Cook at the premiere of Apple TV’s “Ted Lasso” Season 4 at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles on July 27)

schema.headline: Apple Sales Rise 16% in June Quarter to Record $109 Billion, Services Revenue Falls Short of Forecasts

title: NBC Prepares for Spin-Off By Hiring Christopher Halpin as CFO
description:
NBCUniversal is starting to blaze its own corporate path.

	The Comcast-backed media conglomerate, which is slated to be spun off from its parent co
body:
NBCUniversal is starting to blaze its own corporate path.

	The Comcast-backed media conglomerate, which is slated to be spun off from its parent company within a year’s time, named Christopher Halpin as chief financial officer. He will begin in his new role on September 8, and report to Mike Cavanagh, co-CEO of Comcast.

	Halpin had been chief operating officer and chief financial officer at People Incorporated, the Barry Diller-controlled media vehicle that publishes People, Southern Living and InStyle, among other brands. Halpin oversaw duties tied to corporate finance, accounting, M&A, investor relations and administration functions.
	

	“As NBCUniversal prepares to enter its next chapter as an independent public company, we’re thrilled to welcome Chris as our Chief Financial Officer,” said Cavanagh, in a statement. “Chris has spent his career helping build and grow leading businesses across sports, media and entertainment — the areas that will drive NBCUniversal’s growth in the years ahead. He brings deep industry experience, outstanding judgment and a collaborative approach that make him a trusted partner. I can’t think of a better person to join our leadership team as we build on our strong foundation and shape NBCUniversal’s future.”


	Halpin spent nearly a decade in senior leadership roles at the National Football League, where he served as chief strategy and growth officer. Before joining the NFL,, Halpin was a partner and managing director at Providence Equity Partners, where he supervised transactions across the firm’s media, entertainment and technology investments. He began his career in the Merchant Banking Department of Goldman Sachs & Co. He holds a degree in Economics from Princeton University.
	

	Randy Culbertson, NBCUniversal’s current CFO, is expected to remain part of the company’s leadership team and will move to a new role that is supposed to be announced in coming weeks.

schema.headline: NBC Prepares for Spin-Off By Hiring Christopher Halpin as CFO

title: Electronic Arts Set to Close $55 Billion Go-Private Deal Next Week
description:
Electronic Arts is set to close its previously announced $55 billion go-private deal next week, according to the video game publishing giant.

	In a
body:
Electronic Arts is set to close its previously announced $55 billion go-private deal next week, according to the video game publishing giant.

	In a document filed with the SEC Thursday, the “Battlefield 6” and “The Sims” publisher disclosed: “As of July 30, 2026, all regulatory approvals required to complete the Merger have been obtained. Electronic Arts currently expects the Merger to close on or about the close of trading on August 4, 2026. Completion of the Merger remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the remaining customary closing conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement.”
	

	Last September, publicly traded company EA announced it had entered into a private equity deal with   Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners in an all-cash transaction valued at $55 billion.


	Though the original projected close date for the deal was June 30 (the end of the first quarter of EA’s fiscal year 2027), it has been tied up in regulatory approvals over the past few months.

	Upon completion, EA is expected to remain headquartered in Redwood City, California and continue to be led by Andrew Wilson as CEO.

	EA’s been riding high since the impressive launch of “Battlefield 6” last October, with the title becoming the highest-selling game of 2025. 

	The company’s large catalog of game franchises also includes “Skate”, “EA Sports FC” (rebranded from “FIFA”), “Apex Legends,” “The Sims,” “EA Sports,” “Madden NFL,” “EA Sports College Football,” “Need for Speed,” “Dragon Age,” “Titanfall,” “Plants vs. Zombies” and “EA Sports F1,” among others.

schema.headline: Electronic Arts Set to Close $55 Billion Go-Private Deal Next Week

title: Music Industry Moves: Influence Media Partners to Acquire Anthem Entertainment’s Publishing and Film & TV Assets in $600 Million Deal
description: Influence Media Partners, in collaboration with funds and accounts managed by affiliates of BlackRock, has signed an agreement to acquire substantia
body:
Influence Media Partners, in collaboration with funds and accounts managed by affiliates of BlackRock, has signed an agreement to acquire substantially all of the assets of Anthem Entertainment: its music publishing catalogs, film & TV publishing assets and its portfolio of master recordings, for a purchase price of $600 million-plus.

	The catalogs include more than 24,000 released songs and 60,000+ additional unexploited works, including shares in such such as Britney Spears’ “Oops!… I Did It Again”; Justin Timberlake’s “SexyBack”; Timbaland’s “The Way I Are”; Cody Johnson’s “Til You Can’t”; Rush’s “Tom Sawyer”; OneRepublic’s “Counting Stars”; and others from songwriters Jordan Davis, Shane Profitt, and Chris Janson. The film & TV catalog contains soundtracks from iconic movies and television shows such as the “Spider-Man” franchise, the “Men in Black” franchise, and Lego Ninjago. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to close in Q4 2026.
	

	“This acquisition marks a major milestone for Influence Media and reflects the momentum we’ve built as a platform. Anthem’s catalog extends far beyond hit songs – it’s music that has become woven into iconic moments, films, and shows that audiences around the world know and love,” said Lylette Pizarro McLean, Influence Media Founder & Co-Managing Partner. “We’re proud to welcome these works into the Influence portfolio as we continue our next chapter of growth with the support of BlackRock, and look forward to collaborating with our industry-leading partners to create new opportunities and drive exposure for the works and the artists behind them.” Influence Media Partners’ portfolio includes DJ Khaled, Future, and Enrique Iglesias.
	

	Paul Braude, CIO of Direct Private Opportunities Group at BlackRock, said: “Anthem’s catalog exemplifies the high-quality, scaled intellectual property assets we seek within Direct Private Opportunities at BlackRock. Influence Media has built a differentiated platform with deep industry expertise and strong talent relationships, and we are pleased to broaden our partnership through this transaction.”

	Jason Klein, CEO of Anthem Entertainment Inc., said: “Over two decades, Anthem has built a rich and diverse catalog of songs, recordings, and film and television music.  It has been a privilege to serve as custodian of this extraordinary music over the past three years, and I am proud of the dedication and integrity my team has brought to realizing its value.” 

	Truist led the debt financing raise to support the transaction and served as financial advisor to Influence.  Influence was advised by Alter, Kendrick & Baron; McDermott Will & Schulte; and McCarthy Tétrault. BlackRock was advised by Clifford Chance and Stikeman Elliott. Goldman Sachs served as exclusive financial advisor to Anthem, and Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt served as Anthem’s legal counsel.

	+ Sony Music Publishing has promoted Ari Gelaw to Senior Vice President, Creative A&R. Gelaw will continue to be based out of the company’s Los Angeles office, reporting to SMP’s President, Head of U.S. A&R Katie Welle.

	In her new role, Gelaw will be responsible for leading the company’s US R&B/Hip-Hop team, spanning SMP’s New York, Atlanta and Los Angeles offices. Since joining SMP in 2022 as Vice President, Creative A&R, Gelaw has signed BigXThaPlug, Monaleo, Victoria Monet, Flo, Samara Cyn and J White, while also continuing to work closely with top hitmakers including Mustard, Ink, Yeat, Leon Thomas, Camper and more.

	Welle said, “Ari is an exceptional A&R and incredibly skilled at supporting talent.  Her sharp creative instinct and dedication to songwriters have been key to our growth, and this promotion reflects her continued impact both creatively and as a leader.  I couldn’t be more thrilled to work alongside Ari as we continue to elevate the success of our roster and our team.”

	+ Secretly Distribution has promoted Kristian Downs to Executive Director, Platform Operations, reporting in to COO and Partner Chris Welz. Downs will continue to oversee SD’s Digital Operations team, while providing strategic ownership, governance, and long-term operational direction across SD’s core platform infrastructure.
	

	“Kristian has transformed our digital operations since joining Secretly Distribution six years ago. His strategic vision, technical expertise, and collaborative leadership have been instrumental in building the platforms that support our clients today. As we continue to invest in our technology and infrastructure, we’re thrilled for Kristian to be leading the next phase of our platform development.”

	+ Veteran executive Mike Rittberg has left his role as President of Global Distribution at HYBE, where he led commercial partnerships, retail strategy, supply chain, international marketing, and physical production. His previous roles over the years include Warner Bros. Records, Verve Records, Bill Silva Management and Big Machine Label Group, where he served as COO. His roles span artist development, marketing, distribution, retail, promotion, and global partnerships. He can be reached at mikerittberg@gmail.com.

title: Amazon Q2 Ad Revenue Up 26% as Tech Giant’s Profit Booms to $62.6 Billion on Anthropic Investments
description: Amazon reported its second-quarter 2026 earnings Thursday, revealing it beat Wall Street’s estimates with more than $200 billion in revenue for the
body:
Amazon reported its second-quarter 2026 earnings Thursday, revealing it beat Wall Street’s estimates with more than $200 billion in revenue for the April-June period.

	Advertising services revenue for the quarter was up 26% year over year to $19.8 billion, while the tech giant’s overall profit jumped to $62.6 billion largely thanks to its investment in AI company Anthropic.

	Wall Street forecast earnings per share (EPS) of $1.82 on $196.43 billion in revenue, according to analyst consensus data provided by LSEG. Amazon reported diluted EPS of $5.75 on $200.6 billion in revenue.
	

	“AWS is booming, growing 36.7% year-over-year in Q2—our fastest growth in 18 quarters—and our AI and Chips businesses each eclipsed run rates of more than $25 billion,” Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said in a letter to shareholders. “In Stores, we again set record delivery speeds for Prime members in the first half of the year—over 40% more items delivered same-day or overnight, with Grocery and Everyday Essentials growing meaningfully faster than the rest of the business. And, Advertising had another strong quarter with 26% year-over-year growth. There’s a lot to be excited about, and we have much more coming for customers in the second half of the year and beyond.”


	More to come…

schema.headline: Amazon Q2 Ad Revenue Up 26% as Tech Giant’s Profit Booms to $62.6 Billion on Anthropic Investments

title: Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board
description:
After serving for more than 11 years on Netflix‘s board, Anne Sweeney is departing as a director.

	Netflix disclosed Sweeney’s departure in an SEC
body:
After serving for more than 11 years on Netflix‘s board, Anne Sweeney is departing as a director.

	Netflix disclosed Sweeney’s departure in an SEC filing Thursday. “On July 26, 2026, Anne Sweeney notified Netflix, Inc. (the ‘Company’) that she was resigning from the Board of Directors of the Company effective as of that date. Ms. Sweeney’s resignation is not due to any disagreement with the Company,” the streamer said in the filing.


	Sweeney, who is the former co-chair of Disney Media Networks and president of Disney/ABC Television Group, joined Netflix’s board in March 2015. She had served on the Netflix board’s compensation committee.
	

	Sweeney’s entertainment experience, spanning more than three decades, included her oversight of Disney’s cable, broadcast and satellite TV properties worldwide for 18 years. During that time, she was charged with launching and running over 118 Disney channels and had oversight over various ABC properties including ABC Television Network, ABC Studios and the Disney ABC Cable Networks Group. Prior to Disney, she was CEO of FX Networks from 1993 to 1996 and spent more than 12 years at Viacom’s Nickelodeon.

	Her exit from the Netflix board comes after co-founder Reed Hastings, who served as CEO for 25 years, officially departed the board as executive chairman following the June 4, 2026, annual shareholders meeting. Netflix said Hastings is leaving the board “to focus on his philanthropy and other pursuits,” which include tending to the Utah ski resort he owns.

	Jay Hoag, Netflix’s lead independent director who has served on the company’s board since 1999, was named chairman of the company. Hoag, who was an early investor in Netflix, has served as a founding general partner at venture-capital firm Technology Crossover Ventures (TCV) since 1995.
	

	At this year’s annual shareholders meeting, Netflix investors overwhelmingly supported Hoag’s reelection to the board, with over 93% of shares voting for him. It was a different story last year: Shareholders in 2025 voted to boot him as a director with 78% of the shares voted on Hoag’s reelection cast against him. That was over displeasure with his poor attendance at board meetings the year prior, with an attendance rate of 50% in 2024. Following that vote, Hoag had proffered his resignation but Netflix’s board rejected it and kept him on as a director.

schema.headline: Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board

title: Live Nation Posts Continued Growth in Second Quarter With $7.7 Billion in Revenue
description: Live Nation continues to post incremental profits with the release of its second-quarter earnings, reporting $7.7 billion in revenue in a 9% increas
body:
Live Nation continues to post incremental profits with the release of its second-quarter earnings, reporting $7.7 billion in revenue in a 9% increase over the same period last year.

	The company saw concert revenue increase by eight percent over the year, with international markets amplifying growth. Operating income for Q2 landed at $522 million, up seven percent from $487 million during the same period last year, while adjusted operating income ticked up two percent from $798.4 million to $817 million year over year.
	

	The global growth of attendance contributed to Live Nation‘s successful quarter, with 143 million tickets sold through mid-July. Internationally, attendance increased by 10 percent to a record 49 million fans. The company is forecasting an overall 10 percent increase in attendance for the year, and plans to open 25 large venues through the end of 2027 that will allow for 15 million additional fans.


	Last quarter, the company disclosed it took a $450 million hit due to legal costs associated with its Department of Justice settlement and litigation with the states, which ended in a jury deciding that Live Nation and Ticketmaster illegally held monopoly power in the ticketing market. But that appeared to be a drop in the bucket for Live Nation, which still managed to increase 12 percent in overall revenue to $3.8 billion in Q1.

	“In a world of endless screens and AI-generated everything, the one thing that can’t be copied is being there,” said Michael Rapino, President and CEO of Live Nation, in a statement. “More artists are on the road than ever — and fans keep choosing to be in the room with them, driving the strongest concert ticket sales we’ve ever seen. More than 143 million tickets have sold through mid-July, over 14 million ahead of last year’s pace, with mid-teens ticket sales growth across all large venue types: stadiums, arenas, and amphitheaters.
	

	“None of this happens without the artists — they make these moments, and we’re grateful to every artist and crew who trust us with their tours,” he continued. “This was a quarter of milestones: nearly 49 million fans attended our shows, Ticketmaster grew adjusted operating income 14%, and all-time-high deferred revenue points to a strong second half. The first-quarter legal accrual will weigh on reported operating income, but we remain on track for double-digit adjusted operating income growth this year — and to compound at that level for years to come.”

schema.headline: Live Nation Posts Continued Growth in Second Quarter With $7.7 Billion in Revenue

title: ‘Devil Wears Prada 2’ Is Officially Streaming on Hulu and Disney+
description: Gird your loins because “The Devil Wears Prada 2” is officially available to stream on Disney+ and Hulu. The sequel grossed $677 million  at the wor
body:
Gird your loins because “The Devil Wears Prada 2” is officially available to stream on Disney+ and Hulu. The sequel grossed $677 million  at the worldwide summer box office.

	If you’re planning an at-home watch party for the buzzy sequel, you can even delivery a variety of festive merch and apparel through Doordash. The delivery service, which has expanded partnerships with a wide range of retailers, offers same-day delivery for the cast recording of the film’s West End performance from Barnes & Noble, pieces from the film’s Old Navy collaboration and more. Of course, you can also order tons of food and snacks (including cheese, to the chagrin of Emily…) through Doordash.
	

	Released theatrically on May 1, “The Devil Wears Prada 2” opened 20 years after the original “Devil Wears Prada” debuted in theaters in 2006. Audiences were first introduced to Andy Sachs (Anne Hathaway) as an assistant to Runway editor-in-chief Miranda Priestly (Meryl Streep). In the sequel, Sachs returns as the magazine’s features editor. Fellow former assistant Emily Charlton (Emily Blunt) is now a high-powered executive at Dior, who controls the advertising money Runway is in need of maintaining after a scandal.

	In addition to Hathaway, Streep and Blunt, Stanley Tucci, Tracie Thoms and Tibor Feldman reprise their roles in the sequel. New cast members include Kenneth Branagh and Patrick Brammall as Streep and Hathaway’s respective love interests, plus Simone Ashley, Lucy Liu, B.J. Novak, Justin Theroux and Pauline Chalamet. 

	“The Devil Wears Prada 2” features a plethora of fashionable looks courtesy of costume designer Molly Rogers, an dcameos galore. Ashley Graham, Donatella Versace, Lady Gaga, Kara Swisher, Jenna Bush Hager, Paige DeSorbo, Hannah Berner and Tina Brown all appear in the film. 
	

	David Frankel, who directed the 2006 film, and Aline Brosh McKenna, who wrote the original screenplay, returned for the sequel along with producer Wendy Finerman. Michael Bederman, Karen Rosenfelt and McKenna executive produced the film.

	Stream the movie online through Disney+ and Hulu here.

schema.headline: ‘Devil Wears Prada 2’ Is Officially Streaming on Hulu and Disney+

title: Urbanworld CEO Stacy Spikes Warns of Guilds Policing Filmmakers After WGA Pulls Sponsorship Over AI Initiative (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
The email came through last week. The follow-up call may as well have been an email.

	“There wasn’t a lot of insight into their full thinking proce
body:
The email came through last week. The follow-up call may as well have been an email.

	“There wasn’t a lot of insight into their full thinking process,” Stacy Spikes, the founder of the film festival Urbanworld, told Variety about the Writers Guild of America East‘s decision not to sponsor the 30th edition of the BIPOC-focused festival in October.

	The decision to end its 12-year partnership with the New York festival stemmed from this year’s incorporation of an “AI Sidebar,” a new initiative launched in partnership with the New School that will feature the festival screening AI-generated films and shorts, along with conversations and tech demos for AI tools. Spikes said he found out about the WGAE’s decision through an email forwarded to him, prompting him to propose a phone call to clarify the move further.
	

	“Given a 10-year relationship, you don’t want it to go up in flames like that,” he said.

	But if not in flames, fractured it was left — the WGAE said its decision would stand. While Spikes acknowledged the guilds that have sponsored the festival don’t write “massive checks,” he worried that the move could impact the pipeline of filmmakers who try to submit their work to the festival — and risk policing them as they navigate a transforming industry.

	“The danger is for people to start to tell creators what tools they can and cannot use is a very slippery slope,” Spikes said. “I think that’s a very hard thing to try and push down on the filmmaking community.”

	The WGAE declined to comment on its decision or make anyone available for an interview. The union has been a vocal critic of the improper use of the technology, launching an #AINeedsHumans campaign to mobilize its members and making AI a pillar of its negotiations with Hollywood studios during its 148-day strike in 2023. 
	

	The guild pulling its sponsorship reflects how AI remains a third rail within the creative community, even as everyone from directors to actors to director-actor-executive hybrids embrace it in different ways. Film festivals have remained a battleground for such acceptance; Cannes banned AI films from this year’s official lineup, banishing projects like “Hell Grind” to its adjacent marketplace, while Tribeca screened the 75-minute AI-generated “Dreams of Violets” during its programming last month.

	Spikes said the move resembled the industry’s earlier consternation surrounding new technology, such as the pivot from film to digital cameras, but that he has “never seen people say you can’t do this, or we’re going to cancel you, or not work with you if you allow filmmakers to do certain things.” The AI category has not been an issue for other sponsors, who Spikes declined to name.

	Still, Spikes maintained he respected the guild and its role in aiding filmmakers, and that the difference between the two laid in what the role of a film festival should be. In his view, Urbanworld wants “make sure that our filmmakers have the best in class as far as tools and talent and everything to compete on the world stage.”

	“How they make their movies is not something that we, you know, we don’t have a dog in that fight,” he said. “We don’t care one way or the other, but we do feel there’s a responsibility that when there’s emerging technologies and they’re starting to use it and they’re having conversations with themselves about it, we try and bring panelists and speakers and people to present both sides of the story.”

	He hopes the guild eventually comes around to AI’s place within the industry — if not for Urbanworld, then for the filmmakers who will grow up using these tools.

	“There’s young kids right now that are playing with this technology that when they get slightly older, you remove your influence if you’ve walked away from the conversation and say, ‘Here’s a guild. Here’s how we will help you get paid. Here’s how we will ensure that you keep your job. Here’s how we will fight for you,’” Spikes said. “Don’t walk away from those conversations.”

schema.headline: Urbanworld CEO Stacy Spikes Warns of Guilds Policing Filmmakers After WGA Pulls Sponsorship Over AI Initiative (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Netflix Hit With $105 Million Suit After Losing Copy of Nicolas Cage WWII Film
description: A film producer sued Netflix for $105 million on Wednesday after the company lost an unencrypted copy of his World War II film “Fortitude,” starring
body:
A film producer sued Netflix for $105 million on Wednesday after the company lost an unencrypted copy of his World War II film “Fortitude,” starring Nicolas Cage and Ben Kingsley.

	Simon Afram, a Swiss businessman, wrote the script and spent seven years and $45 million bringing it to the screen, according to his lawsuit. The complaint states that an associate producer dropped off a digital cinema package at Netflix headquarters in June so that the company could consider whether to buy the rights.
	

	But when the associate producer tried to retrieve the film, Netflix became unresponsive, according to the complaint. More than a week later, after repeated efforts to arrange a pickup, Netflix acknowledged via email that the film had been stolen.


	“This is a first for us,” wrote Sean Berney, director of original film at Netflix. “Unfortunately, someone stole a good amount of drives from our office desks this past week. We’ve been working through this with our security teams to no luck.”

	“Fortitude” has had a troubled history. In 2023, Afram sued director Martin Scorsese, accusing him of pocketing $500,000 to serve as an executive producer and then doing nothing to help get the project off the ground. Scorsese’s lawyers countersued, argued that Afram was a newcomer to the industry with unrealistic expectations. The parties settled out of court the following year.

	Sources at Netflix say it is standard to share unreleased films either via a password-protected link or with an encrypted DCP that could only be viewed with a Key Delivery Message. In a statement, the company said it is not responsible for the failure to take such precautions.
	

	“Netflix disputes any claim that it bears the risk of loss for a film delivered without the proper industry-standard safeguards,” the company said in a statement.

	Afram’s lawsuit argues that his team was following Netflix’s directions, which stated: “If the DCP is encrypted, please have the keys open from the time the asset lands through EOD on 6/16.”

	According to the complaint, the associate producer informed the company that the DCP was unencrypted, and asked that the film be deleted after the screening. The lawsuit argues that Netflix had a responsibility to store the film in a secure location, and not leave it on an office desk where it could be stolen.

	Netflix said in the statement that it is doing what it can to make things right.

	“While we do not own the rights to ‘Fortitude,’ we take content security seriously and have taken extra measures to support the filmmaker and his team,” the company said. “This includes conducting a thorough investigation and offering to monitor known piracy sites for any unauthorized distribution or sale.”

	So far, the sources say, there is no sign that the film has leaked. In his email, Berney suggested that the thieves were probably just selling the drives for scrap.

	Afram’s lawsuit argues that Netflix’s negligence has jeopardized the film’s exclusivity, thus harming its market value. The suit also complains that Netflix has refused to share details of its investigation, or say whether it reported the theft to the police. 

	For its part, Netflix has not been thrilled with Afram’s response to the situation either.

	“We have declined to share anything about our ongoing investigation with the law firm representing Simon Afram, given their hostile attempts to extort money from Netflix over this situation – including immediately demanding $165 million for the film rather than work with us in good faith,” the company said.

schema.headline: Netflix Hit With $105 Million Suit After Losing Copy of Nicolas Cage WWII Film

Michigan Murder-Suicide
                          Three Dogs, Cat Also Found Dead In 'House Of Horror'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 30, 2026
                            11:06 AM PDT
                                                                      |

                                  July 30, 2026

            The Michigan murder-suicide not only saw the shooting deaths of two parents and six children, but also the gruesome deaths of a bunch of pets who were found inside the family's "house of horror" ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Ottawa County Sheriff's Office Captain Jake Sparks tells TMZ ... after police and firefighters responded to the Karolkiewicz house on July 24, they found at least 3 dead dogs and one dead cat inside the home. The pets all died from smoke or fire, and there may have been more pets who perished.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sparks also said the bodies of Kristopher Karolkiewicz, 47, and his wife, Amanda “Mandy” Karolkiewicz, 39, were discovered in their bedroom. The couple's 4 sons and twin daughters -- ranging in age from 5 to 11 -- were found in their bedrooms as well.
      

            The captain said Kristopher used a semi-automatic handgun to kill his family before setting the home on fire and turning the gun on himself. Sparks said Kristopher fired at least 8 shots during his rampage. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Sparks said investigators are combing the neighborhood for video and talking to witnesses, family and friends to piece together a timeline and to drill down on a motive.
      
    
            Earlier this week, TMZ reported that Amanda apparently posted to Reddit messages about an affair Kristopher had years ago that "shattered" her life.

title: Florida Man Dressed as Superman Arrested For Burglary
description:
Florida Man Dressed As Superman
                          It's a Bird, a Plane, The Man of Steal!
body:
Florida Man Dressed As Superman
                          It's a Bird, a Plane, The Man of Steal!!!

                              July 30, 2026
                            12:15 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Don't tug on Superman's cape ... unless he stole some stuff outta your boat ... in that case, call the cops and have him arrested ... like a recent bust down in Florida.
      
    
            According to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office ... a Florida man was recently popped for allegedly stealing power tools from someone's boat cabin ... and the dude was dressed like the Man of Steel when the cuffs were slapped on.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In police body camera footage from the arrest, deputies confront James Tidwell before he could switch back into his Clark Ketamine alter ego ... and the dude straight up says he helped himself to several items from a stranger's boat.
      

            Tidwell was arrested ... and booked on charges of felony burglary of an unoccupied conveyance and first-degree petit theft.
      
    
            He's out of the clink on a $5,500 bond, jail records show.
      
    
            No word if he's back at his Florida Fortress of Solitude.

title: Kim Kardashian Agrees to Forgive Massive Debt Owed by Man Who Lost Lawsuit
description:
Kim Kardashian
                          I'll Let the 6-Figure Debt Slide!!!
body:
Kim Kardashian
                          I'll Let the 6-Figure Debt Slide!!!
                          Man Owed Her After Court Battle
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 30, 2026
                            1:09 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  July 30, 2026
                                1:51 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kim Kardashian has agreed not to collect the six-figure sum a man owes her for losing a lawsuit he brought against her … after he claimed the judgment would ruin him ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... a man named Ivan Cantu sued Kim after she posted his photo when she meant to post the photo of a prisoner with the same name … in an effort to argue for the inmate to be taken off death row. Ivan lost his lawsuit and was ordered to pay Kim's legal fees, but said doing so would financially ruin him.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A legal rep for Kim tells TMZ ... "This is a lawsuit that should never have been filed. The Court agreed and threw it out and ordered that [Ivan Cantu] pay Kim's legal fees. Kim agreed to waive those fees and so [Ivan] has dismissed his case with prejudice."
      

            The non-prisoner Ivan demanded damages from Kim for the alleged harm the post caused him. She denied all claims of wrongdoing and said she deleted the post immediately after discovering it was the wrong picture.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    The court sided with Kim and dismissed all claims. The mogul was awarded $167k in legal fees. Ivan scoffed at Kim's request for legal fees … calling her a billionaire who didn't need the money. He said it would financially ruin him if he had to pay Kim's legal bills.The judge was not convinced and denied his request to reconsider the amount. He filed an appeal of the decision but has now dropped it after working out a deal with Kim.
